description.narrative:
The UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN) was set up in 2012 under the auspices of the current UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon. The purpose of the network is to mobilise universities, other knowledge institutions, and business to support the Sustainable development goals (SDGs) and contribute to practical problem solutions on local, regional and global level. The SDSN focuses on three priority areas:
(i) building a global network of knowledge institutions organized into national and regional SDSNs with a particular focus on strengthening the capacity of institutions in developing countries; (ii) supporting the implementation of the SDGs and the Paris Climate Agreement, through research and policy tools and analysis; and (iii) building a global online SDG Academy for sustainable development to strengthen the capacity of universities.
Sida’s core support to SDSN for the period 2020-2024 comprise in total 40,5 million SEK. The results follow up of with SDSN will in addition to the network's strategy and the contribution's results framework focus on a few jointly identified thematic priorities which will be updated and adjusted over time. Suggested thematic priorities for the first years include biodiversity, statistics, capacity development and partnerships.

This intervention provides core support to the Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN). As stated in the agreement the overall objectives of the core activities are to partner with Sida in supporting the implementation of the SDGs and the Paris Agreement with a focus on three outcomes:
Outcome 1: Successful operationalization of the Sustainable Development Goals and the international agreement to curb human-induced climate change, supported by SDSNs diverse research and policy programs, in particular data and pathways work.
Outcome 2: A strong Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN) comprised of National and Regional SDSNs
Outcome 3: World-class education on sustainable development, accessible to everyone with an internet connection through the SDG Academy, with an increased focus on capacity development and short-term courses.

Sida's support to the SDSN between 2019 and 2023 has enabled the organization to significantly expand its global role in supporting the implementation of the 2030 Agenda, despite a challenging global context - including the COVID19 pandemic, strong geopolitical tensions, wars and climate related crises.
Assessment of Achieved Results and Lessons Learned (2019-2023)
SDSN has delivered strong results across all three Sida-supported outcomes and objectives. Sidas flexible core funding has been repeatedly highlighted as essential for SDSN's ability to innovate, scale and respond to emerging global needs. SDSN points particularly to the "flexible core funding provided by SIDA which has allowed SDSN to develop successful workstreams before the need for such work was recognized by other funders".
Assessment of achieved results against the agreed SDSN Results Framework (outcome 1-3 for the contribution)
Outcome 1: Successful operationalization of the Sustainable Development Goals and the international agreement to curb human-induced climate change.
The overall assessment is that the outcome has been achieved and in some cases results have exceeded initial expectations. Sida's support enabled SDSN to deliver globally influential tools, scientific assessments, and policy contributions that strengthened SDG implementation and climate action. Sida concludes that the support has most likely contributed to SDSN capacity to shape global SDG and climate policy, produce authoritative data tools and influence high-level negotiations.
Key achievements include: Publication of multiple editions of the Sustainable Development Report, regional SDG indices, and the Global Commons Stewardship Index, widely used by governments and UN processes. Establishment of major scientific initiatives such as the Science Panel for the Amazon and Science Panel for the Congo Basin, both of which has influenced high-level political processes. Strengthening of global climate pathways through the Council of Engineers for the Energy Transition (CEET), the Global Climate Hub, ASEAN Green Future, and Net Zero on Campus. Sida also notes that SDSN has made significant contributions to SDG financing debates, especially for vulnerable countries.
Outcome 2: A strong Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN) comprised of National and Regional SDSNs.
Sida's assessment is that the outcome has been achieved; through the strong global expansion and deepened capacity of both national and regional SDSN chapters. Sida's funding has allowed SDSN to expand its global network and strengthen SDG localization efforts. Sida concludes that the support has enabled SDSN to build the worlds largest academic SDG network and strengthen SDG implementation at national and local levels.
Key achievements include: Growth to 55 national and regional networks by 2023. Support to governments preparing Voluntary National Reviews (VNR), including the first EU-wide VNR. SDSN has also delivered local SDG solutions, city indices, climate initiatives, and parliamentary SDG groups. The continuous expansion of SDSN Youth, has engaged thousands of young innovators.
Outcome 3: World-class education on sustainable development, accessible to everyone with an internet connection through the SDG Academy.
Sida's assessment is that the expected outcome has been achieved through major scaling and innovation. Sidas support has likely contributed to the SDG Academy to expand and reach global scale. Sida concludes that the support has contributed to enabling the SDSN to become a global leader in open SDG education, reaching learners worldwide and expanding into accredited degrees and professional training.
Key achievements include: Expansion to 45 MOOCs and hundreds of thousands of learners. Launch of accredited online Masters programs with UCD and Sunway University. SDSN has also developed professional training programs via LinkedIn Learning and UNESCO partnerships. SDSN has in 2023 surpassed 1 million learners globally.
During the contribution period (2019-2023), SDSN achieved several unexpected results that went beyond the original scope of Sida's support. These include unusually strong political influence (especially in the Amazon), rapid establishment of major new scientific and policy initiatives, accelerated global network expansion, significant scaling of digital education, and increased global uptake of SDSNs analytical tools. SDSN also demonstrated institutional resilience and growth despite global crises and the unforeseen and abrupt discontinuation of Sida funding in 2023.
In conclusion Sida's overall assessment is that SDSN has met - and in several areas delivered above - the expected outcomes of the intervention. The partnership has strengthened global SDG implementation, expanded national and regional networks, and scaled world class SDG education. Sida's contribution is assessed to have delivered high strategic value and contributed to global progress on the 2030 Agenda.
Similar conclusions were made from the Sida financed evaluation of SDSN in 2019. The evaluation (Dox 025515/19) provided Sida with an independent assessment in the design of the 2019-2023 agreement, which has now been successfully completed.
SDSN operations has continued to grow beyond Sida's ended core support in 2023.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
